items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: in the pit conducted by Maurice Bramovitz, and I got to talking to William Shuman during rehearsals

ctx.x: Let's see, I think I finished with the Goodman group in 1945, and maybe after that, I got the 400 Restaurant job, and I took a job with -- a staff job with WNEW which had live musicians on staff in those days, it was the leading independent in New York, radio, in 1945, and also I went on the faculty, the summer school faculty of the Juilliard School, teaching jazz piano improvisation, because the new President, William Shuman, had come in and replaced Dean Wedge, And how I happened to be there was that William…

in the pit conducted by Maurice Bramovitz, and I got to talking to William Shuman during rehearsals, and he thought it'd be a good idea for me to come up and join the faculty of Juliard and teach piano jazz improvisation, because many of the students had a strictly classical background, and many of them could not make a living playing classical music after they graduated, and a lot of them were not qualified to be good teachers, but maybe if they got a taste of the jazz music, they might get in to studio work or…

So I was up there about eight years in summer school, and with WNEW about eight, and then I went up to CBS on staff, and I guess that'd be about 1952 or so and I stayed with CBS staff until '55, and of course, at the CBS staff, you know, we had our Saturday afternoon show on the network with you on bass and Jo Jones on drums, and we'd have two guests on each show, and I remember some of the guests were Dizzy, Carmen McRae was a guest at times, and Miss Sarah might have done one or two.
